title: A queen won on board B mates on board A
summary: On board B, B-Black's B@f2+ was taken with Kxf2, which put B-White on top there and sent the bishop to A-Black, who was ahead on board A by the engines' count for nearly all the rest of the game. Follow the queen at the end: on board B, N@e7+ and Nxg6 won B-Black's queen, and A-Black dropped it with Q@h4+ in the mate on board A.
event: HypeBeast 1.1.1 (pre-release build) against HypeBeast 1.1.0, 500,000 nodes a move

result.text: Black on board A mates; the team of A-Black and B-White wins.

moves.note: Its first choice was c4. It expected a piece to reach board A from board B, most likely a knight for Black, and with any arrival castling scored better than c4 by its count, so it castled first. In the end only a pawn reached Black, from fxe3 on board B, and White played c4 on its next move anyway.

lines.note: The engine expected Black to drop its bishop on h5 and take the knight on f3; Black played Be7 instead.
Its first choice: c4 now and castling a move later.

moves.note: Its first choice was h3. It rated it most likely that a pawn would come to it and a knight to Black, and in that case c4 scored about two pawns better than h3. What came was different: B-Black dropped B@f2+ on board B, Kxf2 took the bishop, and it went to Black here, a case the engine gave less than one chance in ten.

lines.note: Black's expected answer Qe6, met by N@d5; Black played Qd8 instead, counting on that bishop.
Its first choice h3, with c4 a move later.

moves.note: Its first choice was Qe6. B-Black had just dropped B@f2+ on board B, and the engine gave about three chances in four that B-White would take that bishop and send it here; with a bishop in hand it preferred Qd8. Kxf2 came at once, and the bishop went in with B@g4 on Black's next move.

This is the bishop from Kxf2 on board B, which A-Black had counted on since Qd8. If nothing more arrived, B@b6 scored slightly higher, but with one more pawn or knight in hand B@g4 scored far better, so B@g4 stayed its choice. A knight came at once: exd5 on board B took one and sent it here.

lines.note: Its expected continuation: h3 and hxg4 take the bishop, and Black answers with P@g3 and gxf2+; in the game Black met h3 with a second bishop, B@c2.

moves.note: Its first choice was Qxc2, taking the bishop just dropped on c2. It expected a pawn to come from board B, and with that pawn in hand P@d7+ scored about five pawns better than Qxc2. The pawn came at once, from exd5 on board B, but the bishop on c2 was never taken and stood there until the mate.

The knight came from board B, where B-Black's Bxg3 had just taken one, as the engine had expected. With nothing more likely to arrive it played its own choice, scored well above N@g5 and Nxe7. Black took it with Bxc5, and White went on with Nxc7+ and Nxe6, taking Black's queen on e6. That queen went to B-Black, who kept it in hand to the end of the game without dropping it.

lines.note: The engine's expected continuation, still about four and a half pawns in Black's favour by its count.
A search that ignores the other board drops the knight on f4 instead; searched the same way, it scored about three pawns worse than N@c5.

moves.note: Its first choice was Be3. It played P@d5 because that move scored much the best if Black received a pawn from board B, which it gave about one chance in three; if nothing arrived, P@d5 was the worst of the four moves it compared. Nothing arrived. Black answered Bxf2+ and, after Kxf2, g3+, and once White took with Kxg3 its own engine saw a forced mate against it.

lines.note: The engine's expected answer, P@h2+ and Bxf2, about eleven pawns in Black's favour by its count.
Its first choice, Be3, offering a trade of bishops.
A longer search prefers B@g3, but searched the same way it scored about two pawns worse than P@d5, so it shows no better move.
Black's own line at its next move, starting Bxf2+ and g3+; in the game White answered g3+ with Kxg3.

moves.note: Its first choice was Raf8+. g3+ scored better in each case where something arrived from board B, and far better if a queen came, which it gave about one chance in five. The queen came: on board B, Nxg6 took B-Black's queen and sent it here, and after Kxg3 White's engine saw itself mated in five.
The knight dropped with N@e7+ takes B-Black's queen on g6. That queen goes to A-Black, who drops it at the end with Q@h4+; B-Black's recapture hxg6 sends this knight to A-White.

B-White's knight, dropped with check on e7, had just taken B-Black's queen on g6, and that queen went to A-Black. Taking back was far ahead of the alternatives by its count, and it sends the knight to A-White. But by its next move the engine scored this board lost: B-White pushed on with hxg7, and on board A its partner's engine now saw itself mated in five.

lines.note: Its expected continuation: hxg7, and the pawn goes on to promote on h8.
B-White's own line at its next move, starting with hxg7, about fifteen pawns in B-White's favour.

moves.note: By the engine's count, any piece B-White captured here would let A-Black mate on board A, so it counted every loss in its line as a heavy one, and about half of its very low score came from that. In its expected line B-White takes the rook with Nxe8+, and that is what happened a few moves later: Nxe8 sent the rook to A-Black, who had it in hand for the mating attack.

lines.note: Its expected continuation, in which Nxe8+ takes the rook.
A search that ignores the other board takes the knight with gxh5; searched the same way, it scored about two pawns worse than Rhe8.

moves.note: B-Black was lost here, and on board A its partner was being mated. Its first choice was Q@e7, dropping the queen it had held since Nxe6 on board A, but a longer look with the time left over chose Ka8, which scored better if a bishop arrived; one did, from Kxh4 on board A. Most of the very low score is the engine counting that each piece B-White could capture here would let A-Black mate.

lines.note: B-White's expected answer: Bxc7 and Bxd8 take a pawn and a rook.
Its first choice, the queen drop Q@e7.
A search that ignores the other board plays P@e4; searched the same way, it scored about the same as Ka8.

moves.note: With White's king on h4, A-Black's engine found a forced mate starting with this check; Q@f2+ mated just as well by its count. Its expected finish used the queen in hand, the one B-White took on board B with Nxg6.

lines.note: The expected finish: Kg4, Q@g3+ and B@g6+ mate.

moves.note: The queen from Nxg6 on board B comes in with check. By the engine's count every check it considered mated, including R@g3+ with the rook that Nxe8 had sent over from board B; only Bxd3 did not.

lines.note: The expected reply Kxf5 meets B@g6+ mate; White chose Kf3 instead.
A search that ignores the other board mates as fast with B@h5+ and Q@g6+.

moves.note: White's king went to f3 rather than taking the knight on f5, as the engine had expected, and the knight from e6 mates. A drop cannot block a knight check, so the bishop and three knights in A-White's hand were no help, and the team of A-Black and B-White wins.
